stemMd: Two organisms are classified in the same genus but different species. Under the usual taxonomic hierarchy, which statement must be true?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They must belong to different orders.

options.label: B
options.textMd: They must be able to produce fertile hybrids.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They belong to the same family.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They occupy the same ecological niche.

explanationMd: The hierarchy places species within genera, genera within families, and families within orders. Sharing a genus therefore entails sharing its family. It does not prove identical genomes, ecological niches or the ability to produce fertile offspring.

distractorRationale.a: A shared genus lies within one family and order.
distractorRationale.e: Taxonomic grouping does not require genome identity.
distractorRationale.b: Genus membership alone does not establish reproductive compatibility.
distractorRationale.d: Taxonomy does not determine an identical ecological role.
